column1: # Verses where the BSB epub's own red-letter markup is wrong, so the
# quote-propagation heuristic in compile.mjs needs a hand-written correction.
#   1. reference, as "Book chapter:verses"; "verses" takes ranges and singles,
#   2. state: "red" = render as Christ's words, "black" = render as narration
# A "red" row marks every verse body block in the range, including the blocks
# that continue the verse and the words of the characters in a parable.
# Headings and cross-references inside a range are left alone.
# House rule: a parable is Christ's, so the whole of a parable is red even
# where the words belong to a character in the story.
# --- Jesus speaking, but the epub never marked it red --------------------

column3: Giving to the needy and how to pray. Verse 9's "So then, this is how you should pray:" is narration, so it is left out.
Sermon on the Mount continues; verse 28 is narration.
Parable of the Workers in the Vineyard. Verse 17 is narration.
Parables of the Ten Virgins and the Talents, and the Sheep and the Goats.
Good Shepherd speech. Verse 6 ("Jesus spoke to them using this illustration") is narration.
Vine discourse, which runs past the end of verse 26.
Farewell discourse. Verse 17 returns to narration and is left out.
Jesus compares this generation to children.
Letter to Ephesus. The salutation in verse 1 sits in an unmarked block above the red quotation.
Letter to Sardis. The salutation in verse 1 sits in an unmarked block above the red quotation.

column3: God so loved the world and "this is the verdict" are the evangelist's summary. The quotation opened in verse 10 is never closed in the source, so the speech ran on.
